mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and higher borrowing costs, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% MoM indicates a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST drops by more than 10% MoM and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which is a strong indicator of economic distress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a strengthening supply side, which is a positive indicator for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over 3 months signals an easing monetary policy, which is generally positive for equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases over 3 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which is a positive indicator for consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% MoM, it signals strong consumer demand, which is a positive indicator for economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS increases by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tight labor market with high borrowing costs, which is negative for equity markets, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with high borrowing costs
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% and UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
